hero.alt: Guillotine League - The Final Five: Who Survives? The five surviving managers pose with NFL stars in a stadium around a guillotine.

headline.kicker: The Final Five - straight from the group chat
headline.head: "JUST KNOW THAT I OWN THIS LEAGUE"
headline.sub: The commissioner typed it after 186.5, the week's top score by 38.94, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the receiver his team is named after, on bye. Sdobens4 had already written him off ("I thought he was done"). maruniak's ruling: "Dawit talking crazy." Five managers left, and one of them is claiming the building.

offWire.headline: NFL Week 11 inactives, injury tracker: Raiders' Brock Bowers out, Ladd McConkey active for Chargers
offWire.text: The inactives tracker put both of kaelanzm's pass catchers in one headline and said which one was playing. kaelanzm started Bowers anyway, 0.0, and left McConkey on the bench for 20.7. Rarely does the answer key come printed in 20-point type.

kickoff.nudge: Week 12 opens Wednesday night, Packers at Rams at 8pm ET, then Thanksgiving stacks three more: Bears at Lions, Eagles at Cowboys, Chiefs at Bills. Lineups lock game by game, so set Thursday's guys before the turkey goes in.
kickoff.miss: Last week kylereckert started DeVonta Smith (9.1) over Khalil Shakir (15.3). Both play Thursday this time. Choose with a clear head, not a full plate.

paper.benchGem: Sdobens4 started Cam Skattebo (5.8) and benched Ashton Jeanty (27.9). Week 9 it was Jordan Love, Week 10 Stefon Diggs, now Jeanty: three Sundays in a row with a 20-point player hidden. Sam isn't setting a lineup, he's running witness protection.

roast.benched: maruniak kept Travis Kelce (25.4), Mike Evans (22.9) and Parker Washington (18.3) in reserve: 66.6 points that never left the locker room. Parker has now been benched on his 28.2 Sunday and his 18.3 Sunday. That's not a rotation, it's a restraining order.
roast.flop: kaelanzm won Brock Bowers at 3am last Wednesday, $33 to the commissioner's $32. Bowers sat out in Denver. Losing that auction by one dollar was the best thing that happened to the commish all week, and the commish had a 186.5 week.
roast.fresh: This morning maruniak paid $33 for Josh Allen and cut Jayden Daniels to fit him in. Daniels landed on maruniak's roster after the commissioner released him, rode the bench all week (17.06 unused) and is gone again. maruniak picked up the commish's leftovers, never served them, and binned them.
roast.top: JSN's backfield: Jonah Coleman 34.9 (111 yards and three touchdowns against the Raiders), Emmett Johnson 24.3, Breece Hall 19.0. The commissioner won the week on the ground, then walked into the chat to file the deed.
roast.bottom: PumpUpTheJam32 scored 80.46. The perfect lineup off that roster (Purdy at QB, Omarion Hampton and Braelon Allen up from the bench) comes to 97.1, still 6.1 short of fifth. No start/sit regret to argue about. That's the cruel version.
roast.spread: First to last: 106.04 points. Last place scored 80.46. The distance between the top of this league and the bottom was bigger than the bottom.
roast.escape: kaelanzm finished fifth at 103.2, 22.74 clear. That cushion had a name, PumpUpTheJam32, and he cashed out Sunday. Next week there's nobody underneath kaelanzm but the floor.
roast.chopped: PumpUpTheJam32's biggest check was $372 for Jonathan Taylor in the Week 7 waiver run. In the finale Taylor returned 6.7. The last $190 of the budget leaves the league unspent.
roast.bigWallet: kaelanzm has spent $993 of $1,000. Seven dollars left with four rivals and the whole stretch run ahead. The rest of the season gets paid for in couch cushions.
roast.tightWallet: "No number one pick has ever lived up to expectations like Gibbs," posted kylereckert, who took Gibbs first overall and got 27.8 from him Sunday. Kyle also holds $144, the deepest pocket among the living. Satisfied customers rarely leave reviews this loud.

value.stealLine: Dak threw for 325 and four touchdowns, then ran in a fifth.
value.stealJab: JSN paid nothing for 35.9 points, then told the chat he owns the league. Only one of those claims has been verified.
value.lowballLine: Sdobens4 offered $4 for Josh Allen. maruniak paid $33; Sam's bid costs nothing.
value.lowballJab: A Patriots fan bidding four dollars on the Bills' quarterback. Sdobens4 wasn't trying to win, he was trying to insult.

comic.text: You lost Bowers by a dollar and Likely by nine.
comic.label: The league

paper.obituary: PumpUpTheJam32, Week 11. The only manager to leave this league politely.
paper.obituaryNotice: "It's been real folks." Those were the last words of PumpUpTheJam32, posted after 80.46 points left him sixth of six, and they are the most gracious sentence this league has produced in eleven weeks. He went down swinging: beat the commissioner to Derrick Henry on a tiebreak in Week 10, kept bidding when he was the richest survivor, and never once asked for a recount. A little later he added, "today's no fun at all." Correct. It was less fun for him than for anyone.

condolences.msg: We will keep pumping the jam in your name
Thank you for the Josh Allen.
Your tight end is in good hands. Twenty dollars' worth.

jabs.flop: A dollar over the commish for a tight end who never got dressed.
jabs.steal: Zero dollars, thirty-five points. JSN's best purchase didn't cost anything.
jabs.lowball: Sdobens4 bid like he hoped Buffalo wouldn't notice.
